thread:
incident-bot: SEV2: Spike of 401/5xx errors from Okta introspect in us-west-2. Multiple console login failures reported. Alert group: authz-proxy. Pager has been triggered. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/auth-provider-degradation

sam (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Paging PD now. Any front-line customer reports?

pagerduty: Paging sam (oncall) — incident assigned.

maria (sre): I'm seeing a jump in token-introspect timeouts from 12:09 -> 12:35 UTC. Upstream okta-introspect latency 1.2s -> 6.8s, and ~30% 500s in the window. Logs: `authz-proxy` returning 502 -> 401 cascade for SPA console sessions. Sample error from proxy logs: ``ERROR authz/proxy.go: request to https://okta.example.com/introspect returned 502: upstream timeout``

daniel (eng): Is this the JWKS fetch or introspect endpoint? We use introspect for our session validation. JWKS failures would yield different stack traces.

maria (sre): this is introspect. The majority of failures are 5xx from Okta introspect endpoints. JWKS requests are fine.

sam (oncall): can we route traffic to other regions or fall back to a cached token verification path? What's the minimal mitigation to restore console access?

daniel (eng): we have an env flag on authz-proxy to enable local token acceptance using a cached session store (OKTA_INTROSPECT_CACHE=true) — that will accept tokens validated within the last N minutes without calling introspect. It's off in prod. If we flip it, risk is slightly stale invalidations but will restore logins immediately.

maria (sre): +1 for flip as short-term mitigation. Also we can increase introspect client timeouts and retries but that won't help if Okta is returning 5xx.

sam (oncall): do it. Daniel — prepare the rollout commands. Also open a ticket with Okta and attach our logs.

daniel (eng): rolling change: `kubectl set env deploy/authz-proxy OKTA_INTROSPECT_CACHE=true --namespace=prod` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/authz-proxy -n prod`

maria (sre): running the rollout now. Pastie of current pods: ``authz-proxy-5fd7c    Running    Ready 0/1`` (brief).

maria (sre): pods are restarting, applying change to both us-west and us-east for parity.

sam (oncall): monitoring console sign-in metrics (dash: https://console/metrics/authz).

maria (sre): after the restart we see 200s increase for login flow at 12:21 UTC. Errors drop from ~18% -> 2% at 12:24 UTC. Behavior consistent with cache fallbacks working.

daniel (eng): created Okta support ticket #OKTA-2026-451 with attached logs and request for root cause on introspect 5xx spike. Email thread started with account team.

sam (oncall): good. Customer impact note: console sign-in failures affected about 2.6% of active users in us-west during the peak window. A subset of orgs behind strict session invalidation saw failures earlier. Holding page updated: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1938000123

maria (sre): post-mitigations we should also: - add synthetic end-to-end login checks per region - add alert for introspect 5xx rate - add retry budget + exponential backoff in authz-proxy - document fallback TTL tradeoffs in runbook

khari (product): please capture affected customers so CS can proactively reach out if needed. Also include note for enterprise customers on Dedicated/private deployments (they might have different behavior with introspect endpoints).

sam (oncall): assigning follow-ups to the morning rotation: @khari to own customer comms, @maria to own runbook + alerts, @daniel to submit PR to make cache flip safer (add feature flag + gradual rollout).

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread was escalated to SEV2 at 12:10 UTC and mitigated with config fallback at 12:24 UTC. Total mitigation window: ~14 minutes.

maria (sre): Okta replied on ticket: they saw an internal cache invalidation during a deployment causing elevated 5xx for the introspect path between 12:06-12:18 UTC in us-west. They are investigating a permanent fix.

sam (oncall): switching to monitoring-only. Handoff to morning on-call (khari) at 08:00 PDT.

khari (product): ack. I'll handle comms and follow-up tracking.

sam (oncall): quick postmortem items in the thread: 1) Mitigation: enabled OKTA_INTROSPECT_CACHE=true (temporary) 2) Root cause: upstream Okta introspect 5xx spike (Okta investigating) 3) Customer impact: brief login failures for ~2.6% users in us-west, console access primarily affected 4) Next steps: add synthetic checks, tweak retry/backoff, and consider fallback TTL increase.

maria (sre): adding runbook PR link: https://git.redwood/runbooks/auth-provider-degradation/pull/67

incident-bot: Status changed to MONITORING. Reactivate if errors rise above thresholds. :rotating_light:

sam (oncall): thanks team. Closing active paging. Will reopen if Okta reports recurrence.
